blocks.content: Quiz: What does git switch -c feature-x do?
Tap an option below to answer:
Switches to an existing branch called feature-x
The -c flag means create. Without it, git switch feature-x would switch to an existing branch. With -c, it creates the branch first, then switches.
The -c flag means create. Without it, git switch feature-x would switch to an existing branch. With -c, it creates the branch first, then switches.
Creates a new branch called feature-x and immediately switches to it
Correct. The -c flag creates the branch and switches in one step. It is shorthand for running git branch feature-x followed by git switch feature-x.
Correct. The -c flag creates the branch and switches in one step. It is shorthand for running git branch feature-x followed by git switch feature-x.
Deletes the current branch and creates feature-x in its place
git switch -c never deletes anything. It creates a new branch from the current position and leaves the original completely intact.
git switch -c never deletes anything. It creates a new branch from the current position and leaves the original completely intact.
Copies all commits from main into a new branch called feature-x
Branches do not copy commits — they share history up to the branching point and then diverge. No files or commits are duplicated.
Branches do not copy commits — they share history up to the branching point and then diverge. No files or commits are duplicated.
